rows.test_name: Test to order: Dermatology punch biopsies of the mottled/telangiectatic skin lesions (deep punch to subcutis) for H&E and direct immunofluorescence; include bacterial/fungal/AFB stains
rows.gpt5_result:
Dermatology deep punch biopsies (livedoid/telangiectatic lesions and clinically normal skin): Epidermis unremarkable. Numerous small vessels in deep dermis and subcutis (capillaries, postcapillary venules, small arterioles) are distended/occluded by cohesive aggregates of large atypical mononuclear cells with scant cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli; mitoses frequent; occasional intraluminal fibrin thrombi. Minimal perivascular inflammation; atypical cells confined intraluminally. Similar findings present in biopsy of normal-appearing skin.

Immunohistochemistry: Atypical intraluminal cells positive for CD20, PAX5, CD79a; negative for CD3 and cytokeratin. Endothelial markers (CD31/CD34) highlight endothelium encasing intraluminal aggregates. Cells express MUM1/IRF4 and BCL2; CD10 negative; BCL6 weak; subset CD5 positive. Ki-67 proliferation index approximately 95%. EBER in-situ hybridization: negative. Direct immunofluorescence and special stains for bacteria/fungi/AFB: not reported.
rows.astra_result:
Documented histologic findings: Numerous dilated small vessels in the deep dermis and within the subcutaneous fat — capillaries, postcapillary venules, and small arterioles — were distended and largely occluded by cohesive aggregates of large, atypical mononuclear cells. These cells had scant cytoplasm, large vesicular nuclei with coarse chromatin, and one or more prominent nucleoli; mitotic figures were frequent, and apoptotic debris was present. Admixed fibrin thrombi were noted within several involved vessels. There was minimal infiltration of the surrounding dermal or subcutaneous stroma.
Synthetic ancillary results: Direct immunofluorescence showed no specific vascular or dermoepidermal immune deposits. Bacterial, fungal, and acid-fast stains showed no organisms.
